rows.what the ink shows: The initial low bowl and short ascender favor d, but the detached terminal mark over a low stroke can also be a dotted i. The crossed middle does not supply enough separate letter strokes to settle donné against fourni.

The underlined title has a T crossbar and descending stem, followed by an h-like ascending stem and low hump. A separate short vertical stroke at x318–329,y231–257 follows the h and reads as 1; there are no separate rop bowls.

The first cluster preserves tall joined stems but its baseline and ending merge with the cancellation. The following L-like shape, raised hook and descending stem suggest a formula, yet the raised hook has no securely distinct lower stroke of 2 and both parentheses and μ cannot be separately established; the previous narrowed formula was too definite.

The first word begins with a descending p-like curve, then low connected humps and an ending ce-like curl. The second begins with a tall return stroke and continues through small dotted/accented strokes into a low final me/e tail; the compressed letters support puissance deuxième.

Beneath the two heavy cancellation strokes there is one tall looped f with a descender, followed by a narrow parenthetic curve, a short rising t stroke and a final curved closing stroke. No second baseline f or extra power is visible within the deleted group.

An opening curved stroke and a separate closing parenthesis enclose a low mu-like stroke with a descending left segment and rising right shoulder; diagonal and horizontal cancellation strokes cross its middle. The parentheses and surviving lower turn support (μ).

The deleted beginning retains two tall connected strokes for Il. After the intervening space, a small upright loop and a low rightward terminal remain under the cancellation bar, supporting en, though its joining strokes are obscured.

The initial letter has a tall left stroke and a pointed loop descending below the baseline; the rest is covered by a thick horizontal overstroke. The surviving initial can be read as q or p, and the following letters and any i dot do not distinguish qui from par.

The end has a short crossing/downward stroke before the final low hooked letter and a detached rising accent over that last letter. This supports the final té of linéarité; there is no separately visible sequence of m and n humps before a terminal t.
